title: Sort the Shelf
statement: A librarian puts books on a shelf from the thinnest to the thickest. You get the book titles and, at the same positions, their page counts. Return the titles in shelf order: fewer pages first, and when two books have the same number of pages, the title that comes first alphabetically goes first. Titles are unique and use only lowercase letters and spaces.

answerKey.pattern: Sort the indices (or title–pages pairs) with a comparator: by pages, then by title
keyPoints: Keep each title together with its page count, for example by sorting indices or pairs
When pages are equal, it compares titles alphabetically
Return the titles in the sorted order
answerKey.timeComplexity: O(n log n) comparisons (each title comparison is short)
answerKey.spaceComplexity: O(n) for the pairs or indices
edgeCases: All books with the same page count: order by title only
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Insertion sort with the same rule: O(n²), fine for small shelves

hints: If you sort the titles alone, you lose which page count belongs to which title. What can you sort instead?
Sort the positions 0..n-1 (or title–pages pairs). The rule for 'who goes first' looks at pages, then titles.
In the comparator: if the page counts differ, return pages[a] - pages[b]; otherwise compare the two titles.
